mission: Frank v0.1 voll lauffähig auf Andreas PC
workflow: Clay V16 V17 Canonical AST Diff

prior_stage1.question: Was the V16-vs-V17 raw canonical corpus hash mismatch true semantic drift or only grammar-shape representation drift?

evidence: Curated op_add, op_sub and op_ge fixtures differ in raw V16/V17 AST shape but become exactly equal after a guarded normalization that only maps exactly recoverable op_* alias wrappers / operator nodes to the same operator symbol.
Identifier lexing and dotted-prefix scope were explicitly excluded from normalization.
operator_alias_representation.implication: The Stage1 raw-hash equality criterion was too strict for operator wrapper representation alone.

identifier_hyphen_semantics.v16_rule: NAME excludes hyphen so compact subtraction remains lexically visible.
identifier_hyphen_semantics.v17_behavior: Each example is preserved as one NAME token.
identifier_hyphen_semantics.v16_behavior: The same source spelling is tokenized/represented as NAME, '-' operator, NAME ... and therefore changes expression semantics.
identifier_hyphen_semantics.corpus_effect: Both admitted G9/Dialect canonical trees retain residual normalized differences after operator-wrapper normalization.
identifier_hyphen_semantics.implication: V16 cannot currently replace V17 as the declarative grammar without changing admitted corpus meaning or introducing an explicit disambiguation rule.

generic_dotted_prefix_scope.v17: REJECT; V17 deliberately restricts dotted prefix relation handling to Needle.(lowers|owns).
generic_dotted_prefix_scope.implication: V16 is broader than the current V17 declarative contract; this difference must be justified independently rather than normalized away.

external_primary_evidence.source: Lark stable grammar/reference and contextual lexer documentation
external_primary_evidence.relevance: Lark resolves terminal overlap through terminal priorities/longest regex matching and contextual parser expectations; it cannot infer authorial intent when one spelling is intentionally legal both as a hyphenated identifier and as compact subtraction in the same expression context.

hypothesis_result.hypothesis: V16-vs-V17 corpus hash drift is only known operator-wrapper representation and should disappear under a guarded semantic normalization.
hypothesis_result.supported_part: Operator alias wrapper differences are representation-only on tested operator fixtures.
hypothesis_result.refuted_part: Residual admitted-corpus divergence remains because hyphenated identifiers are semantically tokenized as subtraction by V16; generic dotted-prefix scope also differs.
hypothesis_result.strongest_counterhypothesis: Split grammar contracts remain safer until the identifier/subtraction ambiguity and generic dotted scope are explicitly resolved by measured language design rather than hidden normalization.

next_falsifier: Do not run full typed-IR Stage2 yet. First discriminate the hyphen-identifier versus compact-subtraction contract using the admitted corpus and typed-fn/compiler fixtures. Candidate solutions must preserve admitted hyphenated symbolic names AND exact arithmetic operator identity without hidden context-dependent semantic drift. No V18 absent a concrete executable minimal repair candidate.
